Hi Michael -

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps: 

Summary of needs:
- Primary concern: data residency/compliance for customer PII and logs.
- Traffic profile: ~150-250 req/s peak, mostly text generation with occasional long contexts (up to 2k tokens).
- Latency SLO target: median <150ms for standard prompts.
- Cost sensitivity: want to keep inference unit costs predictable for forecasting.

Deployment modes discussed:
- Preferred long-term: Private VPC / on-prem for compliance.
- Short-term path: start with Dedicated reserved capacity to validate traffic and latency, then migrate to Private if controls/attestations required.

Proposed PoC / trial plan (draft):
1) 3-4 week Dedicated trial (reserved capacity) to validate throughput and latency under production-like load.
2) Deliverables: latency/cost benchmark, sample audit logs, model quality check against your eval set, network checklist for VPC peering/KMS.
3) Success criteria: median latency <150ms, 99th percentile <400ms under target load, acceptable cost estimate for projected monthly tokens, security checklist items validated by your InfoSec.

Attachments: Acme_PoC_Trial_Plan_v1.pdf (draft timeline & success criteria).

Can you confirm:
- Stakeholders (security, infra, ML) and the best contacts?
- Whether you can start with Dedicated for the immediate PoC or if you need Private for the trial?
- Any hard constraints on dates - you mentioned aiming for July.

I’ll loop in Dev for the specific network/KMS questions once you confirm stakeholders.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Michael / team -

Quick technical answers and a suggested PoC scope: 

1) Audit logs: For Dedicated we provide per-request metadata (request_id, timestamp, model_id, token_counts, top-level request headers) retained per the contract window and exportable to your S3 or secure logging endpoint. For Private VPC/on-prem, you get full control of logs and retention; Redwood can ship the agent that forwards logs to your SIEM.

2) KMS/HSM: We support Cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) for Dedicated and Private; for Private on-prem we can integrate with customer HSMs via PKCS#11 or dedicated gateway.

3) Network prep: For Dedicated trial we typically do IP allowlist + mutual TLS for callbacks; for Private we do VPC peering or Transit Gateway and an IPsec VPN option. Rajesh - I’ve attached a short network-checklist.csv that lists the common items we need to validate (routes, firewall rules, NAT, peering CIDRs).

Recommended PoC / timeline (target start week of Jul 6):
- Week 0 (prep, 3-5 business days): sign trial SOW, provide network info, KMS config, and sample eval prompts.
- Week 1-2: load test to target 150-250 req/s, run latency benchmarking, collect logs.
- Week 3: model quality checks against your eval set, deliver benchmark report and migration plan to Private if needed.

Success criteria (concrete):
- Median request latency <150ms at target throughput.
- 99th percentile <400ms.
- Audit log export demonstrated to your S3/SIEM.
- KMS encryption for keys in flight and at rest validated.

Attachments: network-checklist.csv; cost-estimate.xlsx (ballpark for projected monthly usage).

If that looks good I’ll create the trial SOW and a short change request that defines rollback/migration timelines.

-Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
